queries.prompt: Run a Direct Connect VIF Layer-3 BGP prefix resilience assessment across our redundant VIFs in both `accepted` and `advertised` directions.
Audit BGP route symmetry across `dxvif-aaa` and `dxvif-bbb` to check for blackhole gaps, partial supernet residuals, and device/location diversity.
Check whether our AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces advertise and receive equivalent CIDR prefixes so failover won't blackhole traffic.

Last month when our primary Mumbai Direct Connect circuit flapped, 4 on-prem subnets went completely unreachable even though our secondary VIF stayed BGP UP. Audit our VIF route tables to see what prefixes are missing on failover.
`VIF-B` advertises `10.10.0.0/22` from on-prem while `VIF-A` only advertises `10.10.1.0/24`—calculate the exact uncovered CIDR space that will blackhole if `VIF-B` fails.
We have two Transit VIFs on two different Direct Connect Gateways terminating at our datacenter—verify that both VIFs advertise the same AWS VPC prefixes back to on-premises.

`ListVirtualInterfaceRoutes` shows `dxvif-01` (`bgpStatus: up`) has 280 accepted routes while `dxvif-02` (`bgpStatus: up`) has 0 accepted routes right after a router maintenance window, and both share `EqMu1`. Assess our failover posture.
Our Direct Connect Resiliency Group connections show `FlatRateTier1` instead of `PortPairFlatRateTier1` and our Transit VIF sits at `199` advertised prefixes—audit our DX VIF failover gaps.
Compare `accepted` and `advertised` prefix sets across our 3-VIF Direct Connect setup (`dxvif-p1`, `dxvif-p2`, `dxvif-dr`) ignoring `0.0.0.0/0` default route masking.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site IPsec VPN connection with BGP over two tunnels to a Virtual Private Gateway and tune IKEv2 phase-1 parameters.
Diagnose why `internal.corp` DNS queries inside `vpc-0167f5c4bb94b89db` time out when both a Route 53 Private Hosted Zone and a Resolver FORWARD rule exist.
Centralize east-west VPC-to-VPC packet inspection through AWS Network Firewall attached to AWS Transit Gateway with `ApplianceModeSupport: enable`.
